subject: Security exhibit — inspection rotation, pen-test notice & evidence POC
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan@healthsync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft security exhibit redlines + inspection rotation

Hi Irene / Karthik —

Thanks for sending the initial MSA + order form. Attached are two files: a proposed redline of the security exhibit and a short SOC 2 summary for our procurement team. A few items we want to confirm before we proceed to legal redlines: 

- Pen-test notice: we typically require ~14 days notice for a penetration test, but can be flexible if Redwood needs a longer scheduling window. Can you confirm Redwood's preferred notice period and whether you allow a short (2-week) pen-test window?
- Inspection scope: HealthSync prefers bounded, sample-based inspections (no full-system dumps). We see language in your draft that allows wider inspection; would Redwood consider explicit carveouts for staging and ephemeral credentials only?
- Evidence cadence: our auditors expect a weekly drop of artifact bundles to a shared Drive during the onboarding period. Can we agree on a POC and an expected upload cadence?
- Access model: ephemeral privileged accounts are ideal; do you allow timeboxed SSH/RDP for pen-test in staging, or do you prefer remote run-throughs only?

If we can lock these elements (notice window, sample-based scope, ephemeral creds, evidence cadence), we can move quickly on our side. Proposed attachments: HealthSync_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.docx, SOC2_Summary.pdf.

Would appreciate a quick 30-min redline call this week if that helps. Proposed times: Thu 10 AM PDT or Fri 2 PM PDT.

Thanks —
Jordan Miller
Senior InfoSec Manager | HealthSync
security@healthsync.com

Attachments: HealthSync_Security_Exhibit_Redline_v1.docx (docx), SOC2_Summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan@healthsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit redlines + inspection rotation

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear asks and the draft redline. High level response below; I also attached a short internal draft (inspection_addendum_draft.docx) that captures the recommended contract language to reconcile both sides.

Summary of Redwood position / proposal: 
- Pen-test notice: we are comfortable with 7–14 days notice. Operationally we ask for a 7-day notice window as our default and will accept a 14-day scheduling window if HealthSync prefers. Final notice period can be captured in the order form.
- Pen-test window: we prefer a bounded window (up to 2 weeks) for active testing in staging. Tests in production are permitted only for specific emergency scenarios with prior written approval.
- Inspection scope: Redwood supports sample-based inspections and will limit access to scoped artifacts only. We propose explicit carveouts for ephemeral staging environments and vendor-specific telemetry that we cannot share (PII redactions).
- Access model: ephemeral timeboxed credentials are acceptable. We will provide jump-host access to a staging environment; we do not permit broad onsite access to internal infra. All privileged sessions will be monitored and recorded.
- SOC 2: we deliver an annual SOC 2 Type II report; customers may request a summary or selected domains in the exhibit.

Next steps and asks from HealthSync: 
1) Confirm preferred pen-test notice (7 vs 14 days) and the proposed July window (Jordan's email below).
2) Confirm evidence upload cadence — we prefer a single POC on each side and weekly evidence drops for onboarding (for steady-state we expect monthly bundles unless otherwise agreed).
3) Agree to an initial 30-min legal + security sync to go over the attach redline and lock the inspection addendum.

We can host the call — Thu 10 AM PDT works for me. Laura, Ben and Karthik are looped for legal / product touches.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Security Operations | Redwood Inference
erine_choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: inspection_addendum_draft.docx (docx)

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit redlines + inspection rotation

Irene —

Thanks for the quick reply and the addendum draft. A couple of clarifying points from our side before the call: 

- We prefer the 14-day notice as a baseline for pen tests, and the July 12–26 window would work for our ops team — can Redwood confirm availability in that period?
- For evidence cadence: weekly uploads during onboarding are fine; we'd like the first three weeks to be weekly, then move to monthly. Can Redwood confirm the format (PDF bundles + raw logs CSV) and whether Redwood will redact PII before upload?
- On ephemeral access: HealthSync prefers that privileged sessions are performed via our test harness; we do not allow recording of application traffic that contains customer data. Can Redwood confirm how session recordings are scoped?

Attaching a short scope outline for the pen test that lists high-level assertions and the test surface (pen_test_scope_outline.xlsx).

If you're available Thu 10 AM PDT, let's meet then and aim to leave the call with agreed language for the exhibit and an action grid for evidence handoff.

Best,
Jordan

Attachments: pen_test_scope_outline.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit redlines + inspection rotation

Irene / Laura —

Quick internal note ahead of Thu: I reviewed Jordan's redline and Irene's addendum draft. Suggested tweaks we should push in the call: 

- Make "notice period" explicit: "Redwood requires minimum 7 days' written notice; HealthSync may request up to 14 days; final scheduling to be agreed in the Order Form."
- Add a sampling table in the exhibit that lists sample sizes by artifact type (logs, config, backups) — drives clarity and limits scope.
- Replace language that permits recordings of traffic with: "Recordings are permitted only for synthetic/test traffic; any capture of production/customer data will be redacted and subject to Data Protection Addendum (DPA) controls."
- Agree to weekly evidence bundles (first 3 weeks) then monthly for steady-state — capture in runbook link.

I'll join the call and have a short redline-ready doc to share.

Thanks,
Karthik
Legal Counsel (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
